adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show a completed `remove_member` spec that asserts anything (the `context ".remove_member"` block is truncated mid-test), so it’s not verifiable that “the new remove_member spec only asserts group.users.count”. Also, even if a spec only checked `group.users.count`, that would be a test coverage critique, not a concrete defect introduced by this diff unless the code is shown to maintain a `user_count` counter cache incorrectly—which is not demonstrated in the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller#create only reads name and visible; the alias_level sent by the client in asJSON() and shown in the form is silently dropped, so new groups always get the default alias level

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, the client’s `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` now includes `alias_level` (and the form binds `alias_level` via the combo-box). `Discourse.Group#create()` POSTs `data: this.asJSON()` to `/admin/groups`. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only sets `group.name` and `group.visible` and never reads/assigns `params[:alias_level]`. As a result, any alias_level chosen in the UI for a new group is ignored and the group will be created with the model/default alias_level instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members does not strip usernames from params[:usernames].split(","), so "bob, alice" fails to find " alice"

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members (new in this diff), usernames is taken as a raw string and split on commas: `usernames.split(",").each do |username| ... User.find_by_username(username) ... end`. No `strip` is applied to each `username`. Therefore an input like "bob, alice" produces " alice" (leading space) and `find_by_username(" alice")` will not match the actual username "alice" (usernames don’t include leading spaces). The finding is directly verifiable from the diff and represents a real correctness issue in the new code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips non-existent users and still returns success, with no error or feedback for partial or total failure

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates over `usernames.split(",")` and only adds a user if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record. Non-existent usernames are simply ignored (no error collected). After the loop it calls `group.save` and, if that succeeds (which it likely will even if no users were added), it returns `success_json`. There is no mechanism to report partial/total failure back to the client, so the finding matches the behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET /admin/groups/:id/users endpoint is removed with no deprecation or alias, a breaking API change for existing consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove an admin route: in `config/routes.rb` the previous member route `get "users"` under `resources :groups` is deleted and replaced with `put "members"`/`delete "members"`. However, the finding claims this is a "breaking API change for existing consumers" and that lack of deprecation/alias is a problem. The removal itself is verifiable, but whether this route is a supported external API requiring deprecation is not established by the diff; it could be an intentional internal admin UI change. Thus the alleged defect (breaking existing consumers) is not directly verifiable from the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public /groups/:name/members response shape changed from a serialized array to {members, meta}, a breaking API change for existing consumers

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`, the `members` action previously did `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`, which returns a top-level JSON array of serialized users. The diff changes it to `render json: { members: serialize_data(...), meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, i.e., a top-level object with `members` and `meta`. That is a concrete response-shape change for the public `/groups/:name/members(.json)` endpoint and would break any existing client that expects an array at the top level.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller#members takes limit from params with no upper bound, allowing a client to pass limit=1000000 and serialize the entire member list

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then applies it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no clamping/maximum. That means a client can request an arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g. 1000000), causing the server to fetch and serialize up to that many group members (and effectively the whole group if it has fewer than that).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Neither limit nor offset is validated in groups_controller#members; a negative offset produces an invalid SQL OFFSET error

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the code takes `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then directly calls `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamping/validation to ensure `offset >= 0`. If a request supplies a negative offset (e.g. `?offset=-10`), `.to_i` will yield `-10` and ActiveRecord will generate SQL with `OFFSET -10`, which PostgreSQL rejects ("OFFSET must not be negative"), causing a 500 error. Although the JS client clamps offset before requesting, the controller itself does not validate it, so the issue is real at the API level.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller#update does not strip group.name (unlike create), so a name like " bob " can be saved via update, inconsistent with create and the username-style name rule

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#create` sets `group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip`, explicitly trimming whitespace. In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, it assigns `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic` with no `.strip`, so update does not normalize names the same way as create. That inconsistency is directly verifiable in the shown code; whether it will ultimately persist depends on model validations not shown, but the lack of stripping in update is a real behavioral difference/defect compared to create.

adjudication_records.issue_text: removeMember reloads with the unchanged offset after removing the last member on the final page, leaving the UI on an empty page with currentPage > totalPages; offset should be adjusted before findMembers()

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Discourse.Group.removeMember`, after a successful DELETE it calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting pagination state. `findMembers` computes the request offset as `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), this.get("offset"))`. If you are on the last page and delete the last member such that `user_count` decreases enough that the current `offset` is now at/after the end (e.g. total 51, limit 50, offset 50 -> delete one => total 50), `user_count` is still the old value when `findMembers` runs, so it will request `offset=50`. The server (`GroupsController#members`) applies `limit/offset` directly and will return an empty `members` array for `offset == total`, leaving the UI on an empty page. This is a verifiable correctness issue introduced by the diff; offset needs clamping (e.g. to `max(0, total-limit)`) before reloading, or after seeing an empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers never clears the usernames input after a successful add (acknowledged TODO), so clicking Add again re-submits the same usernames

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action contains a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment and does not modify `this.get("usernames")` after calling `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))`. The `user-selector` in `group.hbs` is bound to `usernames=usernames`, so the entered usernames remain in the input. Therefore, clicking the Add button again will re-submit the same usernames string (even if the server de-dupes membership, it will still re-send the request).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The promise from addMembers is unhandled, so AJAX failures are silently swallowed

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addMembers` action, the controller calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` and does not return the resulting promise or attach any `.catch`/error handling. That part is verifiable. However, the finding’s stronger claim that “AJAX failures are silently swallowed” is not directly provable from this diff: `Discourse.ajax(...)` may have centralized error handling/logging elsewhere (not shown here), and an unreturned promise is not necessarily “swallowed” in Ember/RSVP (it can still surface via global rejection handlers). So the diff shows no explicit error handling, but not a clearly verifiable silent-failure bug.
